findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime fields
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is selected for the audit-log endpoint, whose ordering key is `datetime`, but this implementation applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the field value. Datetime objects do not support those operations, so building the response cursor raises `TypeError` and the optimized audit-log request fails. Reuse the datetime-to-timestamp conversion used by `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Changing buffer keys to sorted sets breaks existing set keys during rollout
findings.body: Before this change, span-buffer keys were Redis sets; existing keys can remain alive for up to the configured TTL during a rolling deployment. `zcard`/`zunionstore` here, and the corresponding `zadd`/`zscan` operations in the new code, fail with `WRONGTYPE` on those old set keys. Spans already buffered under them can therefore stop processing until expiry, and a rollback has the same incompatibility in the opposite direction. Add a migration/compatibility path or otherwise ensure old-format keys are handled before switching commands.

findings.title: Negative offsets are passed to Django queryset slicing
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled and a cursor has a negative offset, this branch passes that offset directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django querysets reject negative slice bounds rather than interpreting them as reverse-pagination offsets, so the request raises an exception instead of returning a page. Implement reverse traversal with supported query semantics or reject negative offsets explicitly.
